### CVE-2012-0781
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2012-01-18 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 18370: PHP 5.3.8 - Multiple Vulnerabilities (dos/multiple, 2012-01-14, verified=0)

The tidy_diagnose function in PHP 5.3.8 might allow remote attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and application crash) via crafted input to an application that attempts to perform Tidy::diagnose operations on invalid objects, a different vulnerability than CVE-2011-4153.

### CVE-2012-0788
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2012-02-14 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 36682: PHP PDORow Object - Remote Denial of Service (dos/php, 2011-09-24, verified=1)

The PDORow implementation in PHP before 5.3.9 does not properly interact with the session feature, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a crafted application that uses a PDO driver for a fetch and then calls the session_start function, as demonstrated by a crash of the Apache HTTP Server.

Affected:
- n/a / n/a: affected n/a

- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 36789: PHP 5.3.8 - Remote Denial of Service (dos/php, 2011-12-18, verified=1)

### CVE-2012-1823
- Assigner: certcc | Published: 2012-05-11 | Updated: 2025-11-04 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: n/a; CWE-77 CWE-77 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=active, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total
- **CISA KEV**: added 2022-03-25, ransomware=Unknown — PHP-CGI Query String Parameter Vulnerability
- Exploit-DB 29290: Apache + PHP < 5.3.12 / < 5.4.2 - cgi-bin Remote Code Execution (remote/php, 2013-10-29, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 29316: Apache + PHP < 5.3.12 / < 5.4.2 - Remote Code Execution + Scanner (remote/php, 2013-10-31, verified=0)
- Exploit-DB 18834: PHP 5.3.12/5.4.2 - CGI Argument Injection (Metasploit) (remote/php, 2012-05-04, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 18836: PHP < 5.3.12 / < 5.4.2 - CGI Argument Injection (remote/php, 2012-05-05, verified=1)

sapi/cgi/cgi_main.c in PHP before 5.3.12 and 5.4.x before 5.4.2, when configured as a CGI script (aka php-cgi), does not properly handle query strings that lack an = (equals sign) character, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code by placing command-line options in the query string, related to lack of skipping a certain php_getopt for the 'd' case.

Affected:
- n/a / n/a: affected n/a

### CVE-2012-2311
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2012-05-11 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 29290: Apache + PHP < 5.3.12 / < 5.4.2 - cgi-bin Remote Code Execution (remote/php, 2013-10-29, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 29316: Apache + PHP < 5.3.12 / < 5.4.2 - Remote Code Execution + Scanner (remote/php, 2013-10-31, verified=0)
- Exploit-DB 18834: PHP 5.3.12/5.4.2 - CGI Argument Injection (Metasploit) (remote/php, 2012-05-04, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 18836: PHP < 5.3.12 / < 5.4.2 - CGI Argument Injection (remote/php, 2012-05-05, verified=1)

sapi/cgi/cgi_main.c in PHP before 5.3.13 and 5.4.x before 5.4.3, when configured as a CGI script (aka php-cgi), does not properly handle query strings that contain a %3D sequence but no = (equals sign) character, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code by placing command-line options in the query string, related to lack of skipping a certain php_getopt for the 'd' case.  NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2012-1823.

Affected:
- n/a / n/a: affected n/a
